transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. Thanks for seeing me. Well, what made me come in is that, for the past year or so, I just keep getting pulled off track. The smallest thing pulls me off what I’m doing before I can even stop it. Like a phone buzz, or somebody walking past my office. We just moved into this new commercial space downtown, actually. Great square footage, but it's got all these glass walls. My business partner thought it would look more open and collaborative, but honestly, I see every single shadow moving out there. 

Or, I don't know, even a random thought will just derail me. Like, I'll be looking at a spreadsheet and suddenly I'm thinking about my in-laws. Which, don't get me started, they're coming down next month and my father-in-law is already texting me about renting a boat. He always wants to get a pontoon, but he never offers to pay for the gas. It's ridiculous, the guy made a killing in real estate in the nineties but acts like a twenty-dollar gas can is going to bankrupt him. 

But... yeah, what was I saying? Right, I just get pulled away from my work by every little thing before I can catch myself. It's been happening a lot this past year.
Have you had this kind of distractibility since you were a child?

Yeah, looking back, it was definitely around when I was a kid, too. I mean, my teachers were always moving my seat because I talked way too much, or I'd just get up and wander around without asking. 

I remember Mrs. Gable in... I think it was eighth grade? She actually moved my desk right next to her filing cabinet to keep an eye on me. Which was a terrible idea, honestly, because I just spent the whole time reading the labels on her folders. She had this one red folder that just said "Priority" and I always wanted to know what was in it. Probably just, like, detention slips or something. I actually ran into her a few years ago at a Home Depot, buying mulch. She looked exactly the same, just a little grayer. She was looking at the cedar chips, but I told her the dyed black mulch holds its color way better if your yard gets full sun. 

But yeah, I was always blurting things out before they even finished asking a question in class. School just wasn't really built for me, which is probably why I ended up leaving in tenth grade to just start working. Best decision I ever made, honestly. You don't need a piece of paper to know how to build a company from the ground up. I started with just me and a buddy doing junk removal out of an old Ford Ranger... wait, did that answer your question? I kind of lost my train of thought there.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about different things most days?

Worrying? No, not really. I don't really sit around and stew on things. If there's a problem, I just fix it or move on. Like, just last Tuesday, our main supplier for corrugated boxes tried to hit us with a fifteen percent price hike out of nowhere. I didn't even stress about it, I just immediately called up this guy I know in Omaha who runs a packaging plant. 

Great guy, actually. I met him at a trade show in Vegas back in, like, 2018? Man, Vegas is wild. We stayed at the Bellagio, and their buffet used to be absolutely top tier, but that time we went, the crab legs were totally rubbery. You can always tell when they just leave them sitting under those heat lamps way too long. My wife loves crab, but she absolutely refuses to eat it unless we’re actually on the coast somewhere. We took an RV up to Maine a couple years ago just for the seafood, actually. Driving an RV is a lot harder than it looks, by the way, especially trying to park a thirty-footer at a Cracker Barrel... 

But, uh, what did you ask me? Oh, right, worrying. Yeah, no, I'm not really a worrier. I just keep moving.
Do you often feel physically restless or unable to sit still?

Yeah, absolutely. I'm always fidgeting or bouncing my leg. Like, when I'm supposed to sit still, especially during those long family dinners or... oh, I volunteer with the finance committee at our church, and those meetings are brutal. It just feels like there’s a motor running inside me, you know? I just have to move or find something to do with my hands. 

Actually, at the last church meeting, I ended up completely taking apart my ballpoint pen and putting it back together like five times. It was one of those nice metal ones, too, a Pilot G2 Pro. Great pen, honestly, the ink flow is so smooth. I buy them in bulk for the office because the cheap plastic ones always dry out or the caps crack. My business partner, he always chews on the caps of his pens. Drives me insane. I told him he's going to swallow a piece of plastic one day and end up in the ER. 

Speaking of the ER, my youngest son, he's eight, he actually had to go last month because he swallowed a quarter. A whole quarter! Just popped it in his mouth on a dare from his cousin. Kids are unbelievable. The doctor said it would just pass on its own, but my wife was practically having a panic attack the whole time... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, sitting still. Yeah, I just can't do it. I always need to be doing something or moving around.
Before these last year of symptoms, was there any major stressful event or change in your life that seemed to trigger them?

Well, yeah, actually. I mean, I've always been like this, like we talked about, but it's definitely been noticeably harder to manage for, I don't know, about a year and two months now? 

That's right around the time this whole massive conflict with my in-laws started taking over, like, our entire family life. It's just been non-stop drama. My wife's sister, she decided to buy this fixer-upper house right down the street from us, which sounds great in theory, right? Family close by. But she expected me to basically be her free general contractor because I run a business. I told her, look, I do junk removal and logistics, I don't hang drywall. But she got incredibly offended, and then my mother-in-law got involved, and suddenly we're the bad guys because we won't spend our weekends putting up shiplap. 

Shiplap is so overdone anyway, honestly. Every house you see on those home renovation shows has it now. My wife watches those channels constantly. We actually thought about flipping houses once, back before the market got totally crazy. We went to this seminar at a Holiday Inn out by the airport. You know, one of those things where they try to sell you a ten-thousand-dollar coaching package at the end? Total scam. But the coffee they had in the lobby was surprisingly good. Usually hotel coffee tastes like burnt dirt, but this was a really smooth dark roast. I actually asked the guy at the front desk what brand it was, but he had no idea. 

Anyway... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, the stress. Yeah, the in-law thing has just been a huge drain on everything for the last year or so, and it definitely made all this other stuff way harder to deal with.
Have your attention and restlessness been mainly getting worse because of the in-law conflict?

Well, I mean, the in-law stuff definitely made it harder to deal with, but it's not like it just started then. Looking back, this was around when I was a kid, too. My teachers were always moving my seat because I talked way too much, or I'd just get up without asking, or I'd blurt things out before they even finished the question. 

I remember my fifth-grade teacher, Mrs. Henderson, she used to put my desk literally right next to hers. She had this huge wooden desk, solid oak, I think. Actually, oak furniture is really making a massive comeback right now. We just bought this giant solid oak dining table for the house. We had to hire three guys just to carry it through the front door because it weighed like four hundred pounds. One of the guys actually scraped the doorframe, which was incredibly annoying because I had just paid a guy to paint the trim this specific shade of white. You wouldn't believe how many shades of white paint there are at the hardware store. My wife brought home like thirty little paper swatches—eggshell, alabaster, antique snow... it all looks exactly the same to me. I told her to just pick one so we could get it over with, but she spent three weeks deciding. 

Anyway, uh... what were we talking about? Oh, right, the in-laws and it getting worse. Yeah, so the stress with them just kind of amplified how I've always been since I was little.
Did these problems first begin after the conflict with your in-laws started?

No, no, like I was just saying a second ago, it definitely didn't start with the in-laws. Looking back, this was totally around when I was a kid, too. My teachers were always moving my seat around the classroom because I talked way too much, or I'd just get up without asking, or I'd be blurting things out before they even finished asking the question. 

I spent half my time sitting out in the hallway because of it. Our school hallways always smelled like that really strong industrial floor wax, you know the kind? Like fake lemon and heavy chemicals. We actually use a similar industrial degreaser at the warehouse for my company. I run a hauling and logistics business, which is great, but keeping the warehouse floors clean is a total nightmare with the trucks pulling in and out all day. The tires track in so much mud, especially when it rains. It rained for like four days straight last week, completely ruined my weekend plans. I was supposed to take my boat out to the lake. It’s just a small aluminum fishing boat, but I just put a new outboard motor on it, a Yamaha. Those Yamaha motors are incredibly reliable, way better than the Mercury I had before. The old one kept stalling out right in the middle of the lake. 

Wait, sorry. Did you just ask me the same question? But yeah, no, definitely not just the in-laws. Like I said, it's been happening since I was a little kid in school.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days when you felt unusually energized or overly upbeat, with much less need for sleep than usual?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm pretty high-energy most of the time, but not like... unusually upbeat for days on end without sleeping. I definitely need my sleep. If I don't get at least six hours, I'm totally useless the next day. 

Although, honestly, getting decent sleep has been tough lately because we just got this new mattress. It's one of those memory foam ones that comes rolled up in a box, which is wild to me. How do they compress a whole king-size mattress into a box that small? The delivery guy practically threw his back out carrying it up our front steps. We had to wait 48 hours for it to fully expand before we could even sleep on it, which meant we were stuck on the air mattress in the guest room for two nights. Air mattresses are the absolute worst. They always deflate right in the middle, so you wake up folded in half like a taco. I actually tried to patch a hole in an air mattress once with duct tape. Turns out, duct tape does not fix everything, despite what my dad used to say. He used duct tape on the bumper of his old Ford pickup for like three years. It was this hideous silver stripe across the back of a red truck. 

But yeah, anyway, no, I don't have periods where I'm just buzzing for days without sleep. Just my normal level of busy.
Do you find yourself worrying about a lot of different things on most days?

I mean, not really? I'm not a super anxious guy. I don't sit around worrying about a bunch of random things every day. I'm usually too busy doing stuff to just sit and worry. 

Though I guess I do worry a little bit about the supply chain issues with the business right now. It's been a total headache trying to get parts for our forklifts. We had one down for three weeks waiting on a hydraulic pump. Three weeks! And the guy at the parts distributor was zero help. He just kept saying it was stuck at the port. I actually drove down to the port once, years ago, just to see the shipping containers. It's insane how big those cranes are. They look like giant metal dinosaurs just picking up these massive boxes. My nephew is obsessed with dinosaurs right now. He's four, and he knows the names of all the weird ones, not just the T-Rex. He was telling me about one with a club on its tail... an Ankylosaurus, I think? I bought him this huge remote-control dinosaur for his birthday, but it was so loud it made his dog hide under the couch. The dog is a rescue, some kind of terrier mix, and he's terrified of loud noises. We had a terrier growing up, actually... 

Wait, what was the question? Worrying? Yeah, no, I don't really worry about a ton of stuff on a daily basis. Just normal business stuff, you know?
On most days, do you feel anxious or on edge?

Not really, no. I wouldn't say I feel anxious or on edge most days. I mean, I'm always moving, always doing something, but it's not an anxious feeling. It's just... I just have a lot of energy, you know? 

Like, I can't just sit still. If I sit still too long, my legs start bouncing. It drives my wife crazy when we watch TV. We were watching this documentary the other night about deep-sea diving, which is fascinating, by the way. The amount of pressure down there is unbelievable. They have to use these special submersibles with super thick glass. I don't think I could ever do that, being trapped in a tiny metal ball underwater. I get a little claustrophobic sometimes. Like when I have to crawl under the deck to check the pipes. We had a pipe freeze last winter and it cracked, water everywhere. I had to army-crawl through the mud with a flashlight in my teeth. Reminded me of when I used to play paintball with my buddies back in my twenties. We used to go out into the woods every weekend. I was actually pretty good at it, very quick on my feet. 

But yeah, no, I'm not walking around feeling on edge or anything. Just, you know, always ready to go.
Do you find that you worry a lot about many different things and have trouble controlling that worry?

No, not really. Like I said, I'm not a big worrier. I don't get stuck on things or feel like I can't control it. I mean, I have a lot on my plate, running the company and all, but I don't sit around chewing my fingernails over every little detail. If there's a problem, I just fix it and move on. 

Like last week, the landscaping guys we use at the main warehouse accidentally backed their riding mower into our chainlink fence. Smashed it pretty good. The owner of the landscaping company, Sal, he's a great guy though. He makes his own venison sausage. He actually brought me a whole cooler full of it last November. I've never really gotten into hunting myself, honestly. You have to sit perfectly still in a freezing cold tree stand for like, six hours straight just waiting for a deer to walk by. I would go absolutely out of my mind. I'd much rather be on a snowmobile or a dirt bike, you know? Something with a throttle. I actually rebuilt a 1998 Honda dirt bike in my garage last spring. Took it completely apart down to the frame, repainted it, the whole nine yards. Getting the carburetor tuned right was a nightmare, but man, it runs like a dream now. 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? About worrying? Yeah, no, I don't really have a problem with worrying too much. I just stay busy.
Did anything happen around the time these symptoms worsened that felt traumatic or overwhelming to you?

No, not really. I mean, nothing traumatic or anything like that. Things have just always been kind of... fast-paced for me, I guess. I've always been this way, even back in high school. Well, the part of high school I actually went to before I dropped out to work full-time. 

I started out just sweeping floors at this auto shop, but I learned pretty quick. The owner, this guy named Mike, he had this incredible collection of vintage license plates covering the entire back wall of the garage. He said he'd been collecting them since he was a kid. He had one from every state, even Hawaii and Alaska. I always wondered how you get a car from Hawaii to the mainland. Like, do you put it on a boat? Or a really big plane? I guess a boat makes more sense. I've only been on a boat a few times, mostly just fishing on the lake. My buddy has this pontoon boat, and we took it out last 4th of July. We tried to barbecue on it, but the grill tipped over and all the hot dogs fell in the water. The fish probably loved it, though. 

But yeah, no, nothing traumatic happened. It's just how I've always been. Always on the go.
Before age 12, did you already have these attention or hyperactivity problems?

Yeah, oh yeah, definitely. Looking back, this was all happening when I was a kid, too. I remember my teachers were always moving my seat around the classroom. Like, every other week I was at a new desk because I talked too much, or I'd just get up and wander around without asking, or I'd blurt out the answer before they even finished asking the question. 

Actually, my fourth-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she put my desk right next to hers. She had this giant jar of those peppermints with the red and white stripes on her desk. The ones wrapped in clear plastic? I don't know why, but old people always have those specific mints. My grandmother used to keep them in her purse, and they'd always get covered in purse lint. It's weird how certain smells just take you right back, you know? Like the smell of sawdust always reminds me of my dad's workshop. He used to build these intricate birdhouses. Like, miniature Victorian mansions for birds. It was wild. I tried to help him once, but I didn't have the patience for all those tiny little pieces of wood. I'd rather just build a regular box and be done with it. 

But yeah, I was definitely like this way back then. Always getting in trouble for not sitting still.
Have these symptoms been causing problems at work or in your daily life?

I mean, I’m still keeping up overall. The business is running fine. But yeah, I guess it’s starting to cost me some trust at home, and I can definitely tell I'm wearing down the patience of people at work. Like when we have meetings or those one-on-one mentoring conversations, or even just family plans, and they don’t go the way they should because I'm rushing through it or not paying attention. 

Speaking of meetings, we actually just bought this massive new conference table for the main office. Solid mahogany. It weighs an absolute ton. It took six guys just to get it into the freight elevator, and the delivery driver actually scraped the wall on the third floor getting it out. Which was a huge pain because we just had the whole place repainted. My wife picked out the color, it's called 'Agreeable Gray' or something like that. She has a really good eye for design. She wanted to do interior decorating years ago but ended up in real estate instead. The housing market is completely nuts right now, anyway. People are paying cash, way over asking price, waiving all the inspections. My buddy Dave just sold his place and bought a massive RV to drive around the country. He's got this huge diesel pusher, it looks like a rock band's tour bus. I don't know if I could drive something that big, honestly. Trying to parallel park that thing at a gas station must be a total nightmare. 

Wait, what did you ask? Oh, right, problems at work and stuff. Yeah, so it causes some friction when I mess up the schedule or can't sit through a conversation, but like I said, I'm still managing things okay for the most part.

doctor.question: Did these problems first begin after the conflict with your in-laws started?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Looking back, this was around when I was a kid too—teachers were always moving my seat because I talked too much, got up without asking, or blurted things out before they finished the question.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking to clarify when the symptoms first began, specifically checking if they are a recent development or if they have been present since childhood, which aligns with the criterion for onset prior to age 12.

patient.answer:
No, no, like I was just saying a second ago, it definitely didn't start with the in-laws. Looking back, this was totally around when I was a kid, too. My teachers were always moving my seat around the classroom because I talked way too much, or I'd just get up without asking, or I'd be blurting things out before they even finished asking the question. 

I spent half my time sitting out in the hallway because of it. Our school hallways always smelled like that really strong industrial floor wax, you know the kind? Like fake lemon and heavy chemicals. We actually use a similar industrial degreaser at the warehouse for my company. I run a hauling and logistics business, which is great, but keeping the warehouse floors clean is a total nightmare with the trucks pulling in and out all day. The tires track in so much mud, especially when it rains. It rained for like four days straight last week, completely ruined my weekend plans. I was supposed to take my boat out to the lake. It’s just a small aluminum fishing boat, but I just put a new outboard motor on it, a Yamaha. Those Yamaha motors are incredibly reliable, way better than the Mercury I had before. The old one kept stalling out right in the middle of the lake. 

Wait, sorry. Did you just ask me the same question? But yeah, no, definitely not just the in-laws. Like I said, it's been happening since I was a little kid in school.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a distinct period of elevated or irritable mood suggestive of mania/hypomania, which would argue against uncomplicated ADHD and anxiety-related diagnoses.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period lasting several days when you felt unusually energized or overly upbeat, with much less need for sleep than usual?

target_item.reason: The doctor is screening for manic or hypomanic episodes (e.g., feeling unusually energized, decreased need for sleep), which is not covered by the patient's ADHD symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm pretty high-energy most of the time, but not like... unusually upbeat for days on end without sleeping. I definitely need my sleep. If I don't get at least six hours, I'm totally useless the next day. 

Although, honestly, getting decent sleep has been tough lately because we just got this new mattress. It's one of those memory foam ones that comes rolled up in a box, which is wild to me. How do they compress a whole king-size mattress into a box that small? The delivery guy practically threw his back out carrying it up our front steps. We had to wait 48 hours for it to fully expand before we could even sleep on it, which meant we were stuck on the air mattress in the guest room for two nights. Air mattresses are the absolute worst. They always deflate right in the middle, so you wake up folded in half like a taco. I actually tried to patch a hole in an air mattress once with duct tape. Turns out, duct tape does not fix everything, despite what my dad used to say. He used duct tape on the bumper of his old Ford pickup for like three years. It was this hideous silver stripe across the back of a red truck. 

But yeah, anyway, no, I don't have periods where I'm just buzzing for days without sleep. Just my normal level of busy.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether there is persistent excessive worry to distinguish generalized anxiety disorder from ADHD or adjustment-related symptoms.
doctor.question: Do you find yourself worrying about a lot of different things on most days?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about excessive worry, which is a symptom of generalized anxiety disorder, but this is not part of my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
I mean, not really? I'm not a super anxious guy. I don't sit around worrying about a bunch of random things every day. I'm usually too busy doing stuff to just sit and worry. 

Though I guess I do worry a little bit about the supply chain issues with the business right now. It's been a total headache trying to get parts for our forklifts. We had one down for three weeks waiting on a hydraulic pump. Three weeks! And the guy at the parts distributor was zero help. He just kept saying it was stuck at the port. I actually drove down to the port once, years ago, just to see the shipping containers. It's insane how big those cranes are. They look like giant metal dinosaurs just picking up these massive boxes. My nephew is obsessed with dinosaurs right now. He's four, and he knows the names of all the weird ones, not just the T-Rex. He was telling me about one with a club on its tail... an Ankylosaurus, I think? I bought him this huge remote-control dinosaur for his birthday, but it was so loud it made his dog hide under the couch. The dog is a rescue, some kind of terrier mix, and he's terrified of loud noises. We had a terrier growing up, actually... 

Wait, what was the question? Worrying? Yeah, no, I don't really worry about a ton of stuff on a daily basis. Just normal business stuff, you know?

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has pervasive excessive worry, which would support generalized anxiety disorder over ADHD or adjustment disorder.
doctor.question: On most days, do you feel anxious or on edge?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling anxious or on edge, which is a symptom of anxiety. My symptom profile only contains ADHD symptoms, so I do not have this symptom.

patient.answer:
Not really, no. I wouldn't say I feel anxious or on edge most days. I mean, I'm always moving, always doing something, but it's not an anxious feeling. It's just... I just have a lot of energy, you know? 

Like, I can't just sit still. If I sit still too long, my legs start bouncing. It drives my wife crazy when we watch TV. We were watching this documentary the other night about deep-sea diving, which is fascinating, by the way. The amount of pressure down there is unbelievable. They have to use these special submersibles with super thick glass. I don't think I could ever do that, being trapped in a tiny metal ball underwater. I get a little claustrophobic sometimes. Like when I have to crawl under the deck to check the pipes. We had a pipe freeze last winter and it cracked, water everywhere. I had to army-crawl through the mud with a flashlight in my teeth. Reminded me of when I used to play paintball with my buddies back in my twenties. We used to go out into the woods every weekend. I was actually pretty good at it, very quick on my feet. 

But yeah, no, I'm not walking around feeling on edge or anything. Just, you know, always ready to go.

doctor.intent: To distinguish ADHD from generalized anxiety disorder by checking for excessive, difficult-to-control worry.
doctor.question: Do you find that you worry a lot about many different things and have trouble controlling that worry?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about generalized anxiety and difficulty controlling worry, which is not part of my ADHD symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No, not really. Like I said, I'm not a big worrier. I don't get stuck on things or feel like I can't control it. I mean, I have a lot on my plate, running the company and all, but I don't sit around chewing my fingernails over every little detail. If there's a problem, I just fix it and move on. 

Like last week, the landscaping guys we use at the main warehouse accidentally backed their riding mower into our chainlink fence. Smashed it pretty good. The owner of the landscaping company, Sal, he's a great guy though. He makes his own venison sausage. He actually brought me a whole cooler full of it last November. I've never really gotten into hunting myself, honestly. You have to sit perfectly still in a freezing cold tree stand for like, six hours straight just waiting for a deer to walk by. I would go absolutely out of my mind. I'd much rather be on a snowmobile or a dirt bike, you know? Something with a throttle. I actually rebuilt a 1998 Honda dirt bike in my garage last spring. Took it completely apart down to the frame, repainted it, the whole nine yards. Getting the carburetor tuned right was a nightmare, but man, it runs like a dream now. 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? About worrying? Yeah, no, I don't really have a problem with worrying too much. I just stay busy.

doctor.intent: To assess whether there is evidence of a recent traumatic event or stressor causing symptoms, which would support an adjustment disorder rather than ADHD or generalized anxiety disorder.
doctor.question: Did anything happen around the time these symptoms worsened that felt traumatic or overwhelming to you?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about traumatic or overwhelming events that may have triggered or worsened the symptoms, which is an assessment for trauma-related disorders. My symptom profile does not include any trauma-related symptoms.

patient.answer:
No, not really. I mean, nothing traumatic or anything like that. Things have just always been kind of... fast-paced for me, I guess. I've always been this way, even back in high school. Well, the part of high school I actually went to before I dropped out to work full-time. 

I started out just sweeping floors at this auto shop, but I learned pretty quick. The owner, this guy named Mike, he had this incredible collection of vintage license plates covering the entire back wall of the garage. He said he'd been collecting them since he was a kid. He had one from every state, even Hawaii and Alaska. I always wondered how you get a car from Hawaii to the mainland. Like, do you put it on a boat? Or a really big plane? I guess a boat makes more sense. I've only been on a boat a few times, mostly just fishing on the lake. My buddy has this pontoon boat, and we took it out last 4th of July. We tried to barbecue on it, but the grill tipped over and all the hot dogs fell in the water. The fish probably loved it, though. 

But yeah, no, nothing traumatic happened. It's just how I've always been. Always on the go.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient meets the childhood-onset criterion for ADHD by confirming symptoms were present before age 12
doctor.question: Before age 12, did you already have these attention or hyperactivity problems?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Looking back, this was around when I was a kid too—teachers were always moving my seat because I talked too much, got up without asking, or blurted things out before they finished the question.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the attention and hyperactivity symptoms were present before age 12, which directly maps to the 'Onset prior to age 12 years' requirement.

patient.answer:
Yeah, oh yeah, definitely. Looking back, this was all happening when I was a kid, too. I remember my teachers were always moving my seat around the classroom. Like, every other week I was at a new desk because I talked too much, or I'd just get up and wander around without asking, or I'd blurt out the answer before they even finished asking the question. 

Actually, my fourth-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she put my desk right next to hers. She had this giant jar of those peppermints with the red and white stripes on her desk. The ones wrapped in clear plastic? I don't know why, but old people always have those specific mints. My grandmother used to keep them in her purse, and they'd always get covered in purse lint. It's weird how certain smells just take you right back, you know? Like the smell of sawdust always reminds me of my dad's workshop. He used to build these intricate birdhouses. Like, miniature Victorian mansions for birds. It was wild. I tried to help him once, but I didn't have the patience for all those tiny little pieces of wood. I'd rather just build a regular box and be done with it. 

But yeah, I was definitely like this way back then. Always getting in trouble for not sitting still.

doctor.intent: To distinguish ADHD from adjustment disorder by assessing whether the inattention/restlessness is causing significant impairment in functioning.
doctor.question: Have these symptoms been causing problems at work or in your daily life?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’m still keeping up overall, but it’s starting to cost me trust at home and patience from people at work when meetings, mentoring conversations, or family plans don’t go the way they should.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the symptoms are causing problems at work or in daily life, which corresponds to the functional impairment criterion.

patient.answer:
I mean, I’m still keeping up overall. The business is running fine. But yeah, I guess it’s starting to cost me some trust at home, and I can definitely tell I'm wearing down the patience of people at work. Like when we have meetings or those one-on-one mentoring conversations, or even just family plans, and they don’t go the way they should because I'm rushing through it or not paying attention. 

Speaking of meetings, we actually just bought this massive new conference table for the main office. Solid mahogany. It weighs an absolute ton. It took six guys just to get it into the freight elevator, and the delivery driver actually scraped the wall on the third floor getting it out. Which was a huge pain because we just had the whole place repainted. My wife picked out the color, it's called 'Agreeable Gray' or something like that. She has a really good eye for design. She wanted to do interior decorating years ago but ended up in real estate instead. The housing market is completely nuts right now, anyway. People are paying cash, way over asking price, waiving all the inspections. My buddy Dave just sold his place and bought a massive RV to drive around the country. He's got this huge diesel pusher, it looks like a rock band's tour bus. I don't know if I could drive something that big, honestly. Trying to parallel park that thing at a gas station must be a total nightmare. 

Wait, what did you ask? Oh, right, problems at work and stuff. Yeah, so it causes some friction when I mess up the schedule or can't sit through a conversation, but like I said, I'm still managing things okay for the most part.

inference.note: Symptoms clearly began in childhood, include longstanding inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity across settings, and are causing functional impairment. This rules against primary generalized anxiety or adjustment disorder as the main diagnosis.

opening_question.intent: Open the interview and identify the patient's main presenting concern.
opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Longstanding childhood onset pattern of inattention, impulsive blurting, excess talking, leaving seat/wandering, and motor restlessness that persisted into adulthood and causes functional friction at work and home. Symptoms were present before age 12, have continued for over 6 months, and are not better explained by anxiety, mania, trauma, or a recent stressor.
